output.entity_proposed: Congressional Commission on Agriculture and Fisheries (AGRICOM)
output.proposal: HB No. 2322 proposes to establish a three-year Congressional Commission on Agriculture and Fisheries (AGRICOM) to assess the performance of the agriculture and fisheries sector, review existing policies, strategies and programs, and recommend targeted reforms to strengthen food security and improve coordination among the agencies concerned.
output.alignment: Under Government Organization and Mandates, the review should examine how AGRICOM's proposed functions under Section 11 (Powers and Functions of AGRICOM) fit with those of existing oversight bodies, notably the Congressional Oversight Committee on Agricultural and Fisheries Modernization under RA No. 8435 and the Congressional Oversight Committee on Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage under RA No. 12022, and how its recommendations could support the government's intent to streamline agencies and reduce overlapping mandates under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The bill's primary alignment is with Food Security in the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on climate-resilient and smart agriculture, targeted infrastructure and mechanization, and Farm and Fisheries Clustering and Consolidation (F2C2). It is not among the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda measures for the 20th Congress.
legislative_history: HB No. 2322 was filed in the House of Representatives on July 28, 2025 and is pending with the committee.
No measure proposing a congressional commission on agriculture was identified in the 18th or 19th Congress.
HB Nos. 5129 and 5296 were later filed in the House with near-identical text, under the name Congressional Commission on Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Security.

In the Senate, SB Nos. 1199 and 1345 propose the same commission; the Senate Committees on Agriculture, Food and Agrarian Reform and on Finance recommended SB No. 1624 in substitution of both (Committee Report dated December 16, 2025).
HB Nos. 5106 and 11060 propose a congressional commission on agriculture with a different design and scope.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 2322 seeks to establish a bicameral Congressional Commission on Agriculture and Fisheries (AGRICOM) to assess the performance of the agriculture and fisheries sector, review existing policies and programs, and recommend reforms to ensure food security. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 4 (Creation of AGRICOM) creates the Commission to undertake a comprehensive national assessment of the agriculture and fisheries sector and recommend targeted reforms.
b. Section 5 (Composition of AGRICOM) provides that the Commission shall have 12 members, six each from the Senate and the House of Representatives, including the chairs of the committees on agriculture, fisheries, agrarian reform, economic affairs, environment and climate change, and one Minority member from each chamber, who shall serve without compensation.
c. Section 6 (Executive Director) provides for a full-time Executive Director, appointed by the Commission, with the rank and emoluments of Executive Director IV (Salary Grade 29).
d. Sections 7 to 9 (Technical Secretariat; Philippine Institute for Development Studies as Research Arm; Agriculture and Fisheries Legislation and Policy Advisory Council) provide for a Technical Secretariat headed by the Executive Director, designate the PIDS as research arm, and create an advisory council of experts.
e. Section 10 (Duration of AGRICOM) provides that the Commission shall complete its mandate within three years from its organization.
f. Section 11 (Powers and Functions of AGRICOM) authorizes the Commission to formulate short- and long-term policy and program recommendations, approve the framework and budget of the national review, hold hearings, issue subpoenas, and secure technical information from government agencies.
g. Section 13 (Appropriations) provides that initial funding shall be charged against available appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives, with subsequent requirements included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 2322 may be considered alongside SB No. 1624, the Senate substitute for SB Nos. 1199 and 1345, and HB Nos. 5129 and 5296, which likewise propose a congressional commission to review the agriculture and fisheries sector, as well as HB No. 5106, which proposes a similar commission funded through the General Appropriations Act. The measure aligns with the Food Security priority under the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework. In view of the government's policy to streamline functions and reduce duplication under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), the review should assess whether AGRICOM's proposed functions under Section 11 (Powers and Functions of AGRICOM) address gaps in the oversight mandate established under Sections 114–116 of RA No. 8435 and Section 25 of RA No. 12022, and clarify how responsibilities would be assigned among these bodies.
